**title/T1：** HoloGene: Learning to Lift Sliced Spatial Transcriptomics to Holistic 3D Gene Fields

**abstract/A1：** Spatial transcriptomics (ST) provides spatially resolved gene expression measurements, but most 3D ST datasets are acquired as independently processed 2D sections. Computational approaches span slice registration and integration, explicit or generative interpolation, and coordinate-field modeling. Within the last family, implicit neural representations (INRs) offer a continuous, coordinate-queryable parameterization, but standard isotropic coordinate encodings do not explicitly reflect that serial-section measurements are dense in-plane and sparse along the axial direction. We present HoloGene, an anisotropic conditional INR framework for estimating continuous 3D gene-expression fields from pre-registered ST sections. Its central contribution is an acquisition-aware factorization that couples dense in-plane synthesis with sparse axial evolution using established GAE, FiLM, pseudo-label supervision, and CORAL components. HoloGene compresses high-dimensional expression profiles into a graph-autoencoder latent manifold, uses pseudo-label-derived signature conditioning to provide coarse intra-section context, and applies depth-dependent FiLM modulation to model axial variation. A signature-stratified correlation-alignment regularizer encourages cross-slice covariance alignment in latent features. Using held-out measured sections as cross-sectional references, HoloGene improves reconstruction accuracy and biological preservation metrics compared with general-purpose INRs and adapted spatial-transcriptomics baselines. These results support anisotropic conditional modeling as a practical strategy for estimating 3D expression fields from discontinuous ST sections. Code is available at https://github.com/Szym29/HoloGene.

**title/T1：** Trait Collapse in Text-to-Image Generation: Evaluating and Mitigating Personality Inconsistency in Visual Storytelling

**abstract/A1：** In visual storytelling, a believable character must not only look consistent across scenes but also \\textit{behave} in ways that reflect their personality. Current text-to-image (T2I) models preserve visual appearance effectively, yet consistently fail to maintain personality-relevant behavior---a failure we term \\textit{trait collapse}. We show that conventional metrics (CLIP Score, DINO similarity) are blind to this failure, and that abstract personality descriptors and scene-level emotion labels do not produce consistent improvements over neutral prompts across models. To systematically diagnose trait collapse, we introduce \\textbf{ViStoryBench-Personality}, a story-level benchmark combining an expert-validated Visual Cues Lexicon (Fleiss' $κ= 0.757$) with a six-dimensional metric suite covering personality alignment, cross-scene stability, and behavioral coherence. Evaluating seven T2I systems, we confirm a persistent semantic gap between abstract trait labels and visual evidence, and find that visual identity consistency does not imply personality consistency. To bridge this gap, we propose \\textbf{Trait-Behavior-Visual (TBV)}, a training-free prompting framework that decomposes personality traits into renderable visual constraints. TBV improves Personality Alignment Score by up to $+22.1\\%$, with larger gains in models with stronger language-conditioning capacity.

**内容简述：** 该论文改进 GPTQ 的后训练量化求解器，将 group scale 与整数分配联合局部搜索并可周期性地联合重解，以保持低比特与大分组下的下游准确率。

**排除原因：** 属于纯 LLM 权重压缩的数值优化工作，不涉及视觉或多模态推理中的内部状态、证据获取或停止决策，也未提供可迁移到 LVR 的具体状态或训练线索。

<details>
<summary>来源材料：标题、摘要与备注</summary>

**title/T1：** JointQ: Joint Scale-and-Integer Quantization for Large Language Models

**abstract/A1：** GPTQ is the de facto standard solver for layer-wise post-training quantization (PTQ) of large language models, yet the solver itself has received less attention than weight preprocessing and cross-layer objectives. We target a bottleneck of GPTQ: its greedy procedure optimizes continuous group scales separately from the assignment of discrete integers. Evaluating each integer candidate with its closed-form optimal scale has been used for per-channel quantization; JointQ extends it to group-wise quantization, where a row's scales are coupled through the Hessian, and applies it to refine the GPTQ solution. Each local-search move changes one integer and recomputes its group's optimal scale in closed form, accounting for the other groups through the full Hessian; all scales are periodically re-solved jointly. The search starts from a row-wise selection among scale-refitted candidates including the GPTQ solution, so unregularized JointQ never has a larger layer-wise calibration error than GPTQ. JointQ preserves the GPTQ output format and is thus a drop-in replacement. Across four models and four settings, JointQ improves six-task average zero-shot accuracy over vanilla GPTQ in 14 of 16 comparisons and perplexity in 12 of 16. The mean accuracy gain increases from 0.0044 in W4G128 to 0.1559 in W3 per-channel, and JointQ also improves average accuracy over GPTQ with MSE-based scale search and activation ordering in all eight per-channel comparisons, though rarely in G128. An ablation shows that JointQ's diagonal Tikhonov regularization mitigates severe W3 per-channel perplexity degradation, so the largest gains are not due to the local search alone. Overall, JointQ's primary empirical benefit is downstream accuracy preservation in challenging low-bit and large-group regimes. Code is available in the OneComp library at https://github.com/FujitsuResearch/OneCompression.

**comment/C1：** 49 pages, 4 figures. Code: https://github.com/FujitsuResearch/OneCompression

</details>

**title/T1：** Training-Free Anonymization of Driving Data with Promptable Segmentation and 3D Human Mesh Recovery

**abstract/A1：** Camera recordings for autonomous driving contain faces and license plates that should be anonymized before labeling, sharing, or training. Dedicated detectors can miss small plates and faces behind vehicle glass. We present FM-Anonymize, a training-free anonymization pipeline that combines promptable segmentation, 3D human mesh recovery, and generative replacement. SAM 3 locates people, faces, and vehicles and searches zoomed vehicle crops for plates, occupants, and windows. SAM 3D Body assesses face visibility from head orientation and projects head regions for blurring. Optional diffusion inpainting replaces eligible blurred heads with synthetic faces, guided by estimated pose and keypoints. On PP4AV, the blur pipeline protects 97.8% of faces and 95.5% of plates, the highest privacy recall of all compared methods at their default settings. On our recordings, where the localization thresholds were set, it protects 97.1% of faces and 93.4% of plates, compared with 93.7%/73.0% for UrbanAnonymizer, 42.7%/40.7% for EgoBlur, and 96.6% of faces for deface. Synthetic replacement raises full-body keypoint average precision over blurring from 54.1% to 79.6% on our recordings and from 39.9% to 68.3% on PP4AV. Code and configurations are available on https://github.com/max-a-ai/FM-Anonymize

**arXiv ID：** 2611.20425

**arXiv 学科：** cs.CV

**研究分类：** EXCLUDE · 排除

摘要级简评；深入判断请结合原文人工阅读。

**内容简述：** 该论文将交互式实例分割从单视图扩展到多视图遥感场景，构建约百视角的多视图数据集，并提出基于 3D Gaussians 的方法，用户从任意视图点击目标即可获得跨视图一致的实例分割，可投影到点云实现 3D 分割。

**排除原因：** 属于 3D 遥感场景分割与标注效率工作，点击提示仅用于划定目标区域，未涉及 VLM 内部状态、推理轨迹、证据获取或停止决策，与 latent visual reasoning 主线缺少可核查的借鉴点。

<details>
<summary>来源材料：标题、摘要与备注</summary>

**title/T1：** InterRSGaussian: Interactive Multi-view Instance Segmentation for 3D Remote Sensing Scenes

**abstract/A1：** Remote sensing image segmentation plays a critical role in various applications. Interactive instance segmentation, a specialized task within image segmentation, aims to generate precise segmentation results for target objects based on user input prompts. However, previous studies on interactive instance segmentation primarily focus on single-view images, limiting their ability to comprehensively understand complex 3D remote sensing scenes. In this study, we extend interactive instance segmentation from a single-view to a multi-view framework, which can also be easily converted to a 3D segmentation format, thus achieving more accurate and comprehensive 3D remote sensing scene perception across multiple views. First, we construct a multi-view interactive instance segmentation dataset for remote sensing, comprising five distinct scenes, each captured from about one hundred different views. Second, we propose InterRSGaussian, a novel instance segmentation method based on 3D Gaussians. InterRSGaussian enables users to provide point clicks on target objects from any arbitrary view and generates view-consistent instance segmentation results across all input views without requiring manual annotations. The resulting multi-view segmentation can further be projected onto 3D point clouds for 3D segmentation. To improve training efficiency and segmentation performance, we introduce a prior distillation network for initialization. Overall, this study extends traditional 2D remote sensing scene perception into a 3D multi-view framework, enabling a more comprehensive understanding of target objects in complex environments with user interactivity.

</details>

**title/T1：** UrbanTwin Sim2Real LiDAR Challenge 2026: Site-Calibrated Synthetic Data and Multi-Detector Fusion for Roadside 3D Detection

**abstract/A1：** This report summarizes the work submitted by team arnav007 (submission ID 1054222) for the UrbanTwin Sim2Real LiDAR Challenge (V2X-Real track) at the IEEE BigData Cup 2026. The primary objective is to train 3D detectors for vehicles, pedestrians, and trucks using only synthetic roadside LiDAR data, and to generate synthetic scans that are realistic enough to be indistinguishable from real ones. A CARLA based pipeline is developed and calibrated to the fixed sensor site, accurately modeling the range image, including no-return beams, based on unlabelled real development scans. A combined inference detector, using multiple 3D detectors (VoxelNeXt, PV-RCNN, and SECOND) trained exclusively on synthetic data, is also proposed. Each scan is aligned to the synthetic ground plane and processed through the detectors at multiple ground heights. The resulting bounding boxes are fused using bird's-eye view (BEV) clustering, followed by class-specific post-processing to refine heading, box size, and filter low-confidence detections. The final submission achieved a combined score of 0.8947. The ablation study shows that per-scan ground leveling more than doubled the real-scan mAP, while fusing boxes across different heights and models further improved performance.

<details>
<summary>来源材料：标题、摘要与备注</summary>

**title/T1：** Tabular Foundation Models as Emulators for Forecasting Terrestrial Ecosystem Dynamics

**abstract/A1：** Process-based terrestrial biosphere models such as the Ecosystem Demography (ED) model underpin global carbon budgets, but their cost limits global, high-resolution and scenario-rich simulation. Deep emulators such as DeepED reduce that cost but require task-specific architectures and training. Tabular foundation models offer a different route: TabPFN predicts new rows by in-context learning, without being trained on the task. We compare TabPFN-3.5 with two DeepED baselines, $DeepED\_{LSTM}$ and $DeepED\_{Transformer}$, on CarbonGlobe's overall evaluation, which trains on a uniform 1/16 sample of sites and tests on the other 50,779, predicting the 40-year state of all seven ED outputs. We then test every model, trained on present-day data only, on ED runs forced by SSP1-2.6 and SSP5-8.5 for 2021--2060 in six continental forest regions. With no training, TabPFN-3.5 has the lowest present-day height error of the three models and is within 4% of $DeepED\_{LSTM}$ for soil carbon, but is less accurate for AGB, LAI and the carbon fluxes. In 2060, errors are several times larger than at the same sites under present-day forcing, and every model underestimates the biomass that ED gains. Under SSP5-8.5, TabPFN-3.5 is the most accurate model for height, AGB, soil carbon and LAI, with the lowest AGB error in all six regions, although, unlike ED, it predicts no larger biomass gain than under SSP1-2.6. Under SSP1-2.6, no model is best overall.

**内容简述：** 该论文提出 TCNA（时序卷积网络＋多头注意力）作为半导体晶圆厂并行 DEVS 仿真的代理模型，预测吞吐量与周转时间轨迹，并与 Temporal Fusion Transformer 等架构在相同参数量下比较精度与运行成本。

**排除原因：** 这是纯工业时序预测的仿真代理工作，既不涉及视觉或多模态内部表示，也没有 latent 推理状态、证据获取或停止决策等线索，虽含时间序列建模但无可具体核查的迁移接口，故排除。

<details>
<summary>来源材料：标题、摘要与备注</summary>

**title/T1：** A Temporal Convolutional Network with Multi-Head Attention Model: A Surrogate for Parallel DEVS Semiconductor Fab Simulation

**abstract/A1：** Semiconductor factories process many kinds of wafers organized into lots of various sizes and configurations. Different kinds of machines, each with its own operations, process wafers for hours to days, and the wafers undergo many incremental fabrication steps (with re-entry) and flows spanning days to weeks across connected machines. Fast and accurate predictions of throughput ($TH$) and turnaround time ($TA$) dynamics for individual machines and their combinations are essential for factory operations. To use machine learning methods for this purpose, this paper presents a Temporal Convolutional Network with Multi-head Attention (TCNA) architecture. It uses simulated datasets from a benchmark Parallel DEVS (PDEVS) semiconductor fabrication factory model. The factory processes configurable wafer lots with uniform and sinusoidal wafer arrival profiles and may undergo preventive maintenance. The wafer lot size, arrival profile, and factory maintenance policy are used as static covariates. TCNA is applied to a selected set of simulated discrete-event throughput and turnaround time trajectories. The $TH$ and $TA$ time series predicted by TCNA, evaluated with the common $MAPE$, $MSE$, and $R^2$ measures, show comparable or higher accuracy relative to other model architectures, with similar parameter counts and epoch times; the TCNA model size and execution time are similar to those of other architectures such as the Temporal Fusion Transformer. Although time series predictions are less accurate than high-resolution simulations, they can be deployed at a much lower computational cost. The TCNA achieves orders-of-magnitude speedup over PDEVS simulation with an acceptable loss of accuracy, enabling frequent product scheduling, capacity planning, and maintenance planning.

**comment/C1：** 13 pages, 11 figures, 5 tables

We introduce VAHBench, a benchmark that tests this ability through five short-drama briefs specifying story, characters, dialogue and duration. Agents plan and carry out production using shared generation tools. Evaluation combines video completeness and basic quality with checks of production reliability and reporting accuracy. Across 240 runs covering 48 configurations of general-purpose and video-specific agents, higher quality scores do not necessarily mean more complete delivery. Missing episodes, repeated footage and static filler reveal gaps between producing a video file and fulfilling the brief. Added composition tools help some agents but do not consistently improve performance. VAHBench measures how well agents translate user intent into finished video content and helps identify where that process breaks down.

<summary>来源材料：标题、摘要与备注</summary>

**title/T1：** RoShift: Lazy Shift and Weight-aware Rotation for Activation Sparsity in LLM Inference

**abstract/A1：** Activation sparsity accelerates LLM decoding by skipping unnecessary weight reads and computation. However, SiLU-based LLMs exhibit little natural sparsity, and imposing high sparsity can substantially degrade accuracy. We propose RoShift, a training-free method that transforms activations into sparsity-friendly representations. RoShift introduces lazy shift, which recenters SiLU activation distributions around zero and defers correction to the end of the FFN to obtain additional sparsity. It also reduces sparsification-induced output error through rotation that jointly accounts for activation and weight information. By fusing the corrections required for shifting and rotation, RoShift translates these gains into decoding speedup. At 50% and 60% sparsity, RoShift improves average accuracy over TEAL by 1.60 and 3.29 percentage points, respectively, across five models. It achieves up to $1.72\\times$ decoding speedup over the dense model on an RTX 5090 at 50% sparsity and yields a better accuracy-speedup Pareto frontier than TEAL. Code is available at https://github.com/hulahula3247/RoShift

**title/T1：** Calibrated Functional Prediction from Overlapping Nonlinear Observations

**abstract/A1：** We study prediction of nonlinear audit functionals from scalar observations of a shared hidden table state. For Schur-rational operators, local Gaussian projections yield a common sparse kernel for overlapping tasks, repeated row identities, and cross-row dependence. Shared-state residual samples extend this kernel through a positive-semidefinite feature representation. Positive matrix integration and sample-value enclosures connect the original inputs to the actual saved hybrid prediction. A sorted calibration-role perturbation bound then certifies its complete finite-pool pinball risk. Independent complete-loss selection chooses the ridge, score scale, and residual weight, while task-rank calibration supplies an upper endpoint. Evaluation uses twenty new reference contexts per dataset at two task sizes, giving 400 conditions across ten benchmark populations. The mean dataset complete-loss ratios are 0.9977 to the degree-two kernel, 0.9961 to matched complete-MC shrinkage, and 0.9911 to the retrospective minimum over 174 public configurations. The last ratio has a paired reference-bootstrap interval of \[0.9898,0.9927\]. On 40 profiles at coefficient tolerance $10^{-7}$, Gamma quadrature has a geometric mean cold-time ratio of .0646 to strengthened Arb/Petras integration.

**abstract/A1：** We present SCoRe (Support-Calibrated Role fusion), a framework to utilize two complementary vision foundation model-based (VFM) segmenters for training-free cross-domain few-shot segmentation (CD-FSS). Our approach is based on the observation that current VFMs for CD-FSS possess capabilities where one model locates the correct object, while another model computes the better contour. Our approach uses: 1. a method to identify a VFM segmenter to lead Few-Shot Segmentation (FSS) task for a given concept, 2. a novel deterministic boundary correction method using bands of near- and far-pixels at the lead segmenter's predicted boundary of an object, and 3. a region correction mechanism for the other segmenter to conservatively prune components, fill holes, and bridge short gaps on the lead segmenter's predicted masks to improve accuracy. We evaluate SCoRe using RSRM and FSS-SAM3 across 3,314 matched five-shot episodes from 10 datasets. SCoRe achieves 72.738% foreground mIoU averaged across datasets, a gain of 5.210 percentage points over RSRM (paired 95% CI \[4.618, 5.972\]), with per-dataset gains up to 8.461 points over the strongest standalone method and the best point estimate on 7 of 10 datasets.

**title/T1：** DNA: A Double-Helix Hierarchical Deep Interaction Network Architecture for Industrial Digital Twin

**abstract/A1：** High-fidelity modeling is fundamental to industrial digital twin, yet a trade-off persists between the physical transparency of mechanistic models and the superior predictive power of data-driven approaches. Existing hybrid methods often fail to bridge this gap, suffering from shallow integration and rigid one-shot modeling strategies that struggle with complex industrial systems. To address these issues, we propose a \\textbf{Double-Helix Hierarchical Deep Interaction Network Architecture (DNA)}. Inspired by the double-helix structure of biological \\textit{DNA}, our architecture intertwines mechanistic and data-driven modeling strands through two novel interaction strategies, forming a symbiotic architecture in which the two strands mutually enhance predictive capability. Furthermore, the hierarchical structure of DNA allows it to model complex systems in a multi-stage manner through two tailored deep learning frameworks. We evaluate the proposed approach on two distinct industrial systems, where DNA achieves reductions in MAE of 3.704\\% and 3.175\\%, respectively, compared to the strongest baseline. These results demonstrate the effectiveness of DNA and suggest its potential to provide new insights for the development of industrial digital twins.

**arXiv 学科：** cs.LG、cs.AI、cs.CE、physics.comp-ph

摘要级简评；深入判断请结合原文人工阅读。

**排除原因：** 该文面向参数化非线性 PDE 的物理信息元学习求解，核心是最小二乘输出层与 Newton 线性化加速优化，不涉及视觉或多模态推理中的内部状态、证据使用或停止决策，也无可核查的 LVR 方法线索。

<summary>来源材料：标题、摘要与备注</summary>

**title/T1：** Newton-PINet: A fast physics-informed neural network with Newton linearization for meta-learning nonlinear PDEs

**abstract/A1：** Scientific machine learning has opened new avenues for solving parameterized partial differential equations (PDEs), enabling models to learn a family of PDEs and generalize to unseen instances. In this context, data-driven operator learning methods typically require large training datasets, while physics-informed neural networks (PINNs) suffer from difficult optimization and limited generalization, especially for nonlinear PDEs. We propose Newton-PINet, a physics-informed network enhanced by Newton linearization, offering an effective meta-learning framework for nonlinear PDEs. Newton-PINet (i) employs a physics-informed multilayer network with skip connections, where the output-layer weights are solved by least squares; (ii) adopts a two-stage learning strategy that first leverages gradient-based training to learn robust representations from the available training tasks, and then performs gradient-free fine-tuning on the output layer for fast task-specific generalization; and (iii) incorporates a Newton linearization method to speed up the least-squares iteration for nonlinear PDE problems. On a challenging nonlinear reaction-diffusion benchmark, Newton-PINet achieves up to three orders of magnitude lower relative error than recent neural solvers, while using 16x fewer training tasks and over an order of magnitude less training time (about 5 minutes versus several hours). This work advances the meta-learning of PINNs toward data-efficient, fast, and generalizable physics solvers. The code and datasets are publicly available at: https://github.com/fycAIwj/Newton-PINet.

**comment/C1：** Accepted at NeurIPS 2026

摘要级简评；深入判断请结合原文人工阅读。

**内容简述：** 该论文研究图提示微调（graph prompt tuning）在对抗攻击下的脆弱性，并提出由直接处理与间接放大两部分组成的防御框架以提升提示鲁棒性。

**排除原因：** 内容属于图预训练提示的对抗鲁棒性，虽涉及「提示对不可靠偏置的筛选」这一措辞相似点，但无视觉或多模态推理状态生成、证据获取与决策机制，未见可迁移到 LVR 的具体方法线索，故排除。

<details>
<summary>来源材料：标题、摘要与备注</summary>

**title/T1：** GPromptShield: Elevating Resilience in Graph Prompt Tuning against Adversarial Attacks

**abstract/A1：** The paradigm of \`\`pre-training and prompt-tuning", with its effectiveness and lightweight characteristics, has rapidly spread from the language field to the graph field. Several pioneering studies have designed specialized prompt functions for diverse downstream graph tasks based on various graph pre-training strategies. These prompts concentrate on the compatibility between the pre-training pretext and downstream graph tasks, aiming to bridge the gap between them. However, designing prompts blindly to adapt to downstream tasks based on this concept neglects crucial security issues. By conducting covert attacks on downstream graph data, we find that even when the downstream task data closely matches that of the pre-training tasks, it is still feasible to generate highly misleading prompts using simple deceptive techniques. In this paper, we shift the primary focus of graph prompts from compatibility to vulnerability issues in adversarial attack scenarios. We design a highly extensible shield defense system for the prompts, which enhances their robustness from two perspectives: Direct Handling and Indirect Amplification. When downstream graph data contains unreliable biases, the former directly combats invalid information by incorporating hybrid multi-defense prompts to the input graph's feature space, while the latter adopts a training strategy to bypass the invalid components and amplifies valid part. We provide a theoretical derivation that proves their feasibility, indicating that unbiased prompts exist under certain conditions on unreliable data. Extensive experiments across various scenarios of adversarial attacks indicate that the prompts within our defense system exhibit enhanced resilience and superiority. This paper explores a new perspective in graph prompt learning, offering a novel option for robust prompt tuning in downstream tasks.

</details>

**内容简述：** 提出 EBSG，一种无需训练的扩散模型概念擦除方法，用可编辑的示例图文对将宽泛的不安全概念分解为子概念，在生成过程中施加局部空间引导，并配套基于 VLM 的细粒度安全评测协议。

**排除原因：** 该工作面向 T2I 扩散模型的图像安全擦除，空间引导作用于图像采样与内容抑制，而非推理状态的形成、视觉证据筛选或停止决策，VLM 评测也只是一般安全性打分，与 LVR 主线缺少可核查的具体联系。

<details>
<summary>来源材料：标题、摘要与备注</summary>

**title/T1：** Example-Based Spatial Guidance for Training-Free Concept Erasure in Diffusion Models

**abstract/A1：** Text-to-image (T2I) diffusion models often synthesize policy-violating content, necessitating robust safeguards and rigorous evaluation frameworks. However, current approaches remain largely monolithic in both execution and evaluation, limited to coarse-grained categorization within broad unsafe concepts. Such approaches fail to account for the specific constituent factors of a violation, resulting in weak learning signals and allowing model collapse to bypass safety checks. To overcome these limitations, we propose Example-Based Spatial Guidance (EBSG), a training-free method that utilizes user-editable exemplar packs to provide granular spatial guidance for precise concept steering. Unlike existing methods that coarsely steer the entire image away from a broad concept, EBSG decomposes these categories into specific sub-concepts via exemplar text-image pairs, providing explicit, localized steering signals for more robust safety control. Furthermore, we introduce a vision language model (VLM)-based evaluation protocol that provides a fine-grained assessment, avoiding the pitfall of conventional binary evaluators that permit model collapse to bypass safety checks. Empirically, EBSG achieves state-of-the-art erasure performance across diverse safety datasets and concept categories, spanning four nudity benchmarks, seven I2P harmful-concept slices, and four MJA metaphor categories, while supporting multi-concept removal and transferring to a modern backbone, SD3.

**comment/C1：** Accepted at NeurIPS 2026 (poster). 51 pages, including references, checklist, and appendix

</details>

**abstract/A1：** Pixel art is widely used in games and digital content creation, requiring readable forms, coherent spatial relationships, and harmonious colors under limited resolution and palette constraints. Language models show growing promise in visual creation, yet their pixel art creation capabilities lack systematic evaluation. We introduce PixelBench, formalizing text-to-image generation and instruction-guided editing for pixel art and providing a benchmark for these tasks. We further present a creation environment in which language model agents invoke drawing tools through code to generate and edit pixel art. We assess the quality of generated artwork through human evaluation and employ a multimodal large language model as a judge, validating the agreement between its automated assessments and human preferences. We compare language models and configurations across diverse subjects and canvas sizes. <summary>来源材料：标题、摘要与备注</summary>

**title/T1：** Contrastive Activation-Guided Zeroth-Order Preference Optimisation for Memory-Efficient LLM Alignment

**abstract/A1：** Direct Preference Optimisation (DPO) simplifies reinforcement learning from human feedback, but still relies on traditional backpropagation and its associated activation-memory cost. Zeroth-order (ZO) optimisation avoids backpropagation, yet isotropic perturbations can produce noisy updates for preference objectives defined by differences between chosen and rejected responses. We introduce Contrastive Activation-guided Zeroth-Order Direct Preference Optimisation (CA-ZODPO), which constructs a low-rank search subspace from the activation discrepancy between the chosen and rejected responses in each preference pair. Perturbations are restricted to this subspace, while momentum is maintained in low-rank coordinates to preserve the memory advantages of ZO training. On Qwen2.5-1.5B with Anthropic HH-RLHF, CA-ZODPO outperforms common ZO baselines and remains competitive with first-order DPO in pairwise preference evaluation. It also reduces peak GPU memory by about 59\\% at a sequence length of 2048 while retaining the sequence-length scaling behaviour of zeroth-order training.

**comment/C1：** Accepted at AXIOM Workshop @ NeurIPS 2026

</details>

**abstract/A1：** Reliable recognition of steel surface defects is essential for automated quality inspection, but supervised methods require manually annotated images that are costly to produce. This creates a need for methods that can learn useful defect representations directly from unlabelled surface images. This work presents Defect aware MAE, a label free masked autoencoder for clustering steel surface defects. Each image is divided into 196 patches, with 147 masked and 49 processed by a Vision Transformer encoder. Texture energy based masking preferentially hides structurally informative patches, while a shallow decoder reconstructs HOG descriptors that capture local texture and edge orientation. Strong augmentation and an intermediate layer readout are used to form the final image features. Pretraining uses no class labels, bounding boxes, detection branch, or contrastive loss. On the held out NEU DET split, UMAP followed by Ward clustering achieves 98.6% Hungarian matched accuracy, 0.968 NMI, 0.967 ARI, and 0.838 silhouette score. Under an identical encoder and training schedule, it exceeds a SimCLR contrastive baseline in accuracy, NMI, ARI and silhouette scores across 5 seeds.

**title/T1：** Enhancing Mixed Oil Length Prediction through Graph Representation Learning

**abstract/A1：** During the pipeline transportation of refined oil products, the inevitable formation of mixed oil segments poses considerable economic challenges to pipeline networks. Therefore, it is important to accurately predict the length of these mixed oil segments. Although previous methods have achieved relatively accurate predictions by integrating machine and deep learning algorithms, they ignore the statistical dependencies that remain among real-world mixed oil samples, which degrades model accuracy. To address this issue, we propose a novel Sample Dependencies Incorporated Graph Representation Learning (SDI-GRL) model. By representing samples and pipeline features as nodes of a graph, SDI-GRL connects dependent samples through their shared features, allowing message passing to propagate information across related samples. This graph-based framework allows our model to capture the statistical dependencies among samples absent in prior works. A case study on a mixed oil dataset demonstrates that our SDI-GRL model surpasses the strongest existing approach, reducing both the RMSE and the MAE by more than 10%.

**abstract/A1：** Multiplicative gating improves Transformer feed-forward networks (FFNs), but it reduces intermediate representation width under a fixed parameter budget. This trade-off is particularly relevant to Mixture-of-Experts (MoE) models, where individual experts have limited capacity. We introduce ParGLU, a partially gated FFN that combines SwiGLU and ReLU$^2$ in two parallel branches. ParGLU matches the parameter count and principal matrix computation budget of conventional SwiGLU. We evaluate ParGLU in 30M, 75M, and 152M MoE language models using three random seeds per scale. ParGLU outperforms SwiGLU across all three seeds at 75M and 152M, reducing mean validation NLL by 0.0200 and 0.0249, respectively. Results at 30M are mixed. Controlled ablations show that increasing backbone width or expert width strengthens ParGLU's relative performance. Ablation studies further show that combining SwiGLU and ReLU$^2$ improves performance over either architecture alone. Token-frequency analysis reveals larger improvements on low-frequency tokens. These findings show that fully gated FFNs are not always the most effective use of an MoE expert's parameter budget. Partial gating can improve language modeling in MoE Transformers.

**arXiv ID：** 2611.20698

**作者：** Gaoliang Song、Chengjie Li、Pengju Liu、Chenchen Chang、Jinhao You、Hongzhi Zhang

**arXiv 学科：** cs.CV

[论文页面](<http://arxiv.org/abs/2611.20698v1>) · [PDF](<https://arxiv.org/pdf/2611.20698v1>)

**研究分类：** EXCLUDE · 排除

**优先级：** NONE

摘要级简评；深入判断请结合原文人工阅读。

**内容简述：** 提出 STARS，用级联架构将遥感图像去阴影拆分为阴影区复原与非阴影区恒等两个阶段任务，并设计特征选择融合适配器引入大模型先验。

**排除原因：** 属于纯图像复原的遥感去阴影工作，虽提到按区域拆分职责与掩码先验，但不涉及 VLM 推理状态、证据获取或 latent 表示，缺乏可迁移到 LVR 的具体线索。

<details>
<summary>来源材料：标题、摘要与备注</summary>

**title/T1：** STARS: Stage-Adaptive Responsibility Separation for Shadow Removal in Remote Sensing Images

**abstract/A1：** Shadows are a ubiquitous radiative attenuation phenomenon in remote sensing images and can severely affect high-resolution remote sensing interpretation tasks. In shadow removal, although introducing a mask prior provides explicit positional information for the restoration network, it also causes non-shadow regions to be modulated by the shadow prior, producing a systematic brightness shift; notably, this phenomenon is independent of whether the mask is accurate. In remote sensing images, non-shadow regions usually occupy a larger proportion, so a small shift over these regions incurs a much higher cost on whole-image metrics than an equal gain in shadow regions. Adopting a task-decoupling perspective, we therefore decompose shadow removal into two tasks, shadow-region restoration and non-shadow-region identity, within a cascaded architecture, and handle them sequentially. Based on this insight, we propose STARS, a cascaded shadow removal framework that separates regional responsibilities across stages. The method retains the advantages of the shadow mask while resolving the degradation of non-shadow regions, without requiring a complex parallel dual-branch structure. Meanwhile, to introduce large-model prior knowledge into remote sensing tasks, we further design a Feature Selection and Fusion Adapter (FSFA). We conduct extensive experiments on three benchmark datasets, UAV-SC+, ISTD+ and WSRD+ 2026, demonstrating the superiority of STARS. The framework shows that decoupling regional responsibilities can resolve the intrinsic contradiction of mask priors, providing a new direction for image restoration with region heterogeneity.

**abstract/A1：** Auxiliary products such as flight protection and flexible-change services are recommended alongside primary travel purchases. This setting creates a granularity ambiguity: SKUs within one product type share semantics but differ in price and coverage, while rejecting one offer does not imply disinterest in the entire type. We present \\textbf{PEETS} (\\textbf{P}reference-aware \\textbf{E}mbeddings with \\textbf{E}xplicit \\textbf{T}ree \\textbf{S}tructure), a training-time framework for auxiliary product bundling. PEETS regularizes an existing click--conversion predictor through two conditional comparisons. Hierarchical Contrastive Loss uses the pair's common ancestor as a reference; Negative Contrastive Loss conditions structural sampling and comparison shifts on logged rejection events. Both act on shared SKU representations during training. This separates catalog relatedness from individual preference supervision and leaves the predictive serving path intact. PEETS achieves 78.20\\% AUC, exceeding TWIN V2 by 0.90 percentage points and the matched base model by 1.15 points. In a 14-day online evaluation, gross auxiliary GMV per exposed user-day improves by 8.20\\% over Policies, 3.06\\% over Base, and 0.84\\% over TWIN V2, with all three user-bootstrap 95\\% intervals above zero. Bundling rate is 0.51 points below Policies. The cancellation interval's upper limit exceeds the prespecified margin. PEETS adds no auxiliary-loss computation to serving and records 42.1~ms p95 latency, compared with 42.0~ms for Base.

</details>

**title/T1：** CLIFT: Contrastive LiDAR Instance Features for 3D Pedestrian Tracking

**abstract/A1：** A social robot has to keep track of the people around it over time to plan its motion, a task handled by 3D multi-object tracking. For the LiDAR modality, trackers usually sit on top of a detector and link its detections across frames with a separate motion model or re-identification network. We instead show how a 3D LiDAR detector itself can be turned into a tracker by adding an instance-level contrastive objective on its intermediate voxel features. Each embedding is read from the voxels inside a detected box, and boxes are matched across frames by cosine similarity and the Hungarian algorithm, without a motion model. The detector backbone is fine-tuned together with this objective, which learns identity-aware features while leaving detection accuracy essen- tially intact. Because the method uses only the voxel features that Li- DAR detectors already produce, it is backbone-agnostic. On the JRDB 3D tracking leaderboard our LiDAR-only tracker ranks first on HOTA (38.58) and IDF1 (37.99), 13.04 and 9.30 points above the next pub- lished method, and second on MOTA and OSPA. Code is available at https://hermak56.github.io/CLIFT/.

</details>

**title/T1：** A Seismic Foundation Model for Dense Feature Extraction

**abstract/A1：** Deep-learning-based seismic interpretation is constrained by scarce high-quality annotations, and most existing models are trained separately for individual tasks. We present SeisDFE, a 7B-parameter seismic foundation model for dense feature extraction, pretrained on 5.34 million 2D images derived from more than 500 seismic volumes. A three-stage pretraining strategy, combining discriminative self-supervised learning, Gram feature anchoring, and multi-resolution adaptation, improves feature discriminability while preserving spatial coherence. With its encoder frozen, SeisDFE supports seismic facies classification, salt detection, fault detection, and relative geologic time estimation. It outperforms existing seismic foundation models on all four tasks and a natural-image-pretrained model on all but fault detection, with the largest gains under scarce supervision: using only two annotated sections of the F3 dataset, it improves whole-volume mIoU by 12-19 percentage points over the baselines. The learned features remain effective with task-specific decoders and extend to synthetic-to-field transfer and sparse 3D geobody interpretation. These results show that large-scale seismic pretraining organizes geological information into dense representations that are directly reusable across interpretation tasks.

</details>

**排除原因：** 这是临床远程监测与因果异质效应估计的应用研究，既不涉及多模态模型内部状态、视觉证据使用，也不涉及推理期状态生成或动态计算，缺少可供 LVR 借鉴的具体机制线索。

<details>
<summary>来源材料：标题、摘要与备注</summary>

**title/T1：** Who Benefits from Telemonitoring? Uplift Modelling of a Nationwide Home Blood Pressure Monitoring Programme

**abstract/A1：** Home blood pressure (BP) telemonitoring programmes are being deployed at national scale, yet enrolment resources are finite and the benefit of telemonitoring is unlikely to be uniform across patients. We study the Primary Technology-Enhanced Care for Hypertension (PTEC-HT) programme, a nationwide telemonitoring programme for hypertensive patients in Singapore. Using retrospective data on 16,694 patients registered between August 2020 and May 2024, we first estimate the average treatment effect of the programme on 6-month BP control against a propensity-score-matched non-participant cohort, finding an absolute improvement of 5 percentage points in the rate of BP control (74% vs. 69%, $p = 3\\times10^{-12}$), rising to 12 percentage points (63% vs. 50%, $p = 1\\times10^{-15}$) among patients with uncontrolled BP at baseline. We then move beyond the average effect and apply uplift modelling to estimate individual treatment effects. Across five uplift learners evaluated with 5-fold cross-validation and Qini curves, an uplift random forest performed best on the full cohort and an S-learner on the uncontrolled-baseline subcohort, although performance bands overlapped across learners. On held-out patients, realised uplift was largest in the top predicted-uplift groups and declined across the ranking. These patients had higher baseline BP grade, more recent hypertension diagnosis and lower medication and diagnosis burden, a profile we offer as hypothesis-generating for targeted enrolment. A handcrafted rule built from these features was competitive with the learned models, outperforming all of them on the uncontrolled-baseline cohort, suggesting that uplift models are useful for discovering heterogeneity that can be distilled into simple enrolment criteria for directing limited care team capacity.

</details>

**abstract/A1：** The approach utilizes 10 bands from Sentinel-2 imagery, along with terrain information, in a deep learning pipeline to classify potential hazard sources in any given mountainous region. The performance of our model has been evaluated against the data collected during the rock-ice avalanche event in the Chamoli region in the Indian Himalayas on 7th February 2021. U-Net performs segmentation of the detected land surface in the satellite image, detects changes in the identify candidate hazard zones, and then the following steps are performed to calculate the potential energy using the Monte Carlo sampling for steepest descent (D8) flow paths, finding the exposed structures in the downstream locations, and ranking the zones depending on the risk score. In comparison to the simple spectral rule, our approach achieved the higher macro F1 score of 0.648 (as compared to 0.519). But the F1 score in case of rock and soil was low, being in the range of 0.3s. In case of optical change detection in winter, it's only that northeast-facing slope which couldn't be detected, as it was under 73% of shade prior to the incident. The parameters have been set for this particular scene alone and not independently; hence, this is a retrospective test, and this test locates a failure which has occurred earlier. The primary contribution of this paper is locating the pipeline leak.

摘要级简评；深入判断请结合原文人工阅读。

**内容简述：** 提出 VA-Assembly，一个无需训练的三维部件装配框架：给定单张参考图与固定的部件几何，利用冻结的视角条件扩散模型的分数梯度来优化各部件的平移、旋转与缩放。

**排除原因：** 该工作属图像到三维几何装配，优化对象是显式部件变换参数而非多模态推理的内部 latent 状态，视觉信息仅作为几何对齐条件，未见对推理状态生成、证据获取或停止决策的可核查线索，故排除。

<details>
<summary>来源材料：标题、摘要与备注</summary>

**title/T1：** VA-Assembly: View-Aligned Score Guidance for Training-Free 3D Part Assembly

**abstract/A1：** Image-to-3D foundation models have improved 3D reconstruction, but typically produce monolithic representations without explicit part-level structure. Part-aware generation and learning-based assembly methods often require part-level supervision, category-specific priors, or paired part-layout training data. We instead consider a practical but underexplored setting in which independently prepared or generated 3D parts have no predefined inter-part relationships, shared coordinate frames, or consistent scales, and must be assembled into a reference-consistent object from a single image. We present VA-Assembly, a training-free framework for 3D part assembly through part-level transformation estimation using view-aligned diffusion guidance. Given a reference image and fixed 3D part geometries, VA-Assembly optimizes each part's translation, rotation, and scale. We condition a frozen view-conditioned diffusion model on same-view renderings of a reference-derived monolithic 3D representation, producing score gradients geometrically aligned with the part configuration. This guidance provides multi-view structural cues under large initial misalignment. By repurposing pretrained visual-structural priors as transformation-level supervision, VA-Assembly requires no annotated part layouts, predefined part taxonomies, category-specific assembly training, or bounding-box-based layout initialization. Experiments compare VA-Assembly with geometric registration and compositional layout baselines using each baseline's supported transformation components, showing improved part-wise transformation estimation. Ablation studies show that view-aligned conditioning, rather than diffusion guidance alone, is critical for reliable transformation gradients. Updating only part transformations preserves explicit component separability and supports component-level editing, replacement, and reconfiguration.

**comment/C1：** 16 pages, 9 figures

</details>

**排除原因：** 属于图像复原与生成式输出质量的训练方法，不涉及视觉推理状态、证据筛选、动态计算或停止决策；其特征分布匹配监督针对像素输出的感知质量，与 LVR 的 latent 内容使用和贡献分配缺少可核查的具体线索，故排除。

<details>
<summary>来源材料：标题、摘要与备注</summary>

**title/T1：** An Efficient Training Paradigm for Image Restoration via Improved Fréchet Loss

**abstract/A1：** Diffusion-based image restoration achieves strong perceptual quality but typically relies on iterative sampling, leading to slow inference. Existing single-step methods often use diffusion distillation or adversarial training, complicating optimization. To simplify training, we propose FDIR, a framework for training single-pass generative restoration models through regression-style supervised optimization using directly computable objectives. To realize this paradigm, FDIR employs the Fréchet distance to match the feature distributions of restored and real images in frozen representation spaces, providing explicit distribution-level supervision. To better accommodate image restoration, we incorporate local patch features to capture fine-grained restoration discrepancies. Moreover, we introduce instance-adaptive statistics by combining the feature moments of each SR-HQ pair with synchronized historical statistics, allowing distribution matching to incorporate input-specific correspondence while retaining distribution-level context. FDIR optimizes only the LoRA parameters of the restoration backbone. Experiments demonstrate strong perceptual restoration quality and efficient training, suggesting a simpler paradigm for generative image restoration.

摘要级简评；深入判断请结合原文人工阅读。

**内容简述：** 该文是一篇哲学论证，借语言语用学、拉康镜像理论、鲍德里亚拟像、西蒙东个体化与皮尔斯符号学，主张与 LLM 的对话是真实的会话活动而非模拟，并提出「混合符号制造」以描述人、模型、语料与技术装置共同参与的意义生成。

**排除原因：** 讨论的是人机会话的本体论与符号学地位，不涉及视觉或多模态推理的内部表示、latent 状态、证据获取或训练监督，也未提供可迁移的方法线索，与 LVR 主线缺乏实质联系。

<details>
<summary>来源材料：标题、摘要与备注</summary>

**title/T1：** Conversing with a Conversational Agent: A Real Conversation, Not a Simulated One

**abstract/A1：** The claim that interactions with artificial conversational agents merely simulate human conversation rests on a philosophical distinction between reproducing the observable features of an activity and actually performing it. Although this distinction is appropriate for certain physical phenomena, its application to linguistic and symbolic activities is far less straightforward. This article argues that conversations with large language model (LLM)-based agents are genuine conversational activities rather than mere simulations, without thereby attributing consciousness, subjective understanding, or human intentionality to artificial systems. Drawing on the distinction between subjective and objective simulation, the article first examines the limitations of defining conversation exclusively through the intrinsic properties of its participants. It then develops a relational and semiotic account of conversational activity, informed by linguistic pragmatics, Lacan's Conversing with a Conversational Agent theory of the mirror, Baudrillard's concept of the simulacrum, Simondon's philosophy of individuation, and Peirce's semiotics. These perspectives make it possible to distinguish the reality of conversational interaction from the appearance of artificial subjectivity and from the epistemic validity of the meanings produced. The argument culminates in the concept of Hybrid Semiotic Fabrication, which characterizes meaning-making as a distributed process involving human participants, artificial intelligence, corpora, and technical arrangements. Recognizing the reality of human-AI conversation therefore entails neither anthropomorphizing artificial agents nor granting their outputs epistemic authority. Rather, it requires a more precise account of the relational, semiotic, and normative conditions under which conversational meaning is produced and justified.

</details>

**title/T1：** Vision-Language Model-Based Phase-OTDR Event Classification

**abstract/A1：** Phase-sensitive optical time-domain reflectometry (Phase-OTDR) enables distributed vibration sensing, but reliable event classification has traditionally relied on fully supervised models that require extensive annotated data. This study examines the adaptability of a Vision-Language Model (VLM) for Phase-OTDR event recognition through few-shot learning. Raw samples are converted into Short-Time Fourier Transform (STFT) dB-magnitude spectrogram mosaics, color-mapped and resized to RGB images, and processed by a Contrastive Language-Image Pre-training (CLIP) image encoder; few-shot adaptation optimizes only the Tip-Adapter-F cache keys, leaving both encoders unchanged. Under a leakage-controlled protocol (train-side support/validation pool of 512 images per class, fixed held-out test of 120 per class, no test-set access during selection, 20 distinct support-sampling trials), the selected configuration (the ViT-L-14 Vision Transformer encoder with OpenAI weights, 128 shots per class) reaches 96.81 +/- 0.42% accuracy and a macro-averaged F1 score of 96.79 +/- 0.42% on the held-out test set; a label-efficient 16-shot setting, that is, 96 labeled support images at adaptation time across the six classes, already attains 90.17 +/- 0.81%. Tip-Adapter-F clearly outperforms both zero-shot CLIP and the standard training-free Tip-Adapter, and prompt and backbone analyses show that performance is stable across Vision Transformer encoders and insensitive to prompt wording at the selected operating point. Overall, CLIP visual features carry a transferable structure that a lightweight support cache turns into a label-efficient Phase-OTDR event classifier. The code and the corresponding image dataset are made publicly available on GitHub to support further research: https://github.com/miralab-ai/vlm-phase-otdr.

**内容简述：** 该论文发布开源 Python 包 artist，基于 PyTorch 实现太阳能塔式电站光路的端到端可微数字孪生，用于从实测光斑反演定日镜面形与运动学参数并优化瞄准点。

**排除原因：** 虽使用可微光线追踪做逆问题求解，但对象是聚光电站光学工程，不涉及视觉语言推理中的内部状态、证据筛选或停止决策，缺乏可核查的借鉴线索。

<details>
<summary>来源材料：标题、摘要与备注</summary>

**title/T1：** artist: A Python package for differentiable ray tracing and gradient-based optimization of solar tower power plant operation

**abstract/A1：** Solar tower power plants provide dispatchable, renewable energy by concentrating sunlight with thousands of mirrors, called heliostats, onto a central receiver. Efficient operation requires accurate modeling of the optical path from each heliostat to the receiver and compensation for manufacturing imperfections, kinematic misalignment, and material degradation that distort the flux distribution. Conventional ray tracers predict the flux from an assumed plant model but are limited to forward simulation. They cannot recover unknown plant parameters from measured flux nor directly optimize plant operation. We present artist, an open-source, FAIR4RS-compliant Python package implementing a fully differentiable digital twin of solar tower power plants. By making the optical pipeline, comprising heliostat surface representation, kinematics, blocking, and ray tracing, end to end differentiable, artist turns the digital twin from a passive forward model into an active physics-based tool for inverse modeling and data-driven optimization. The resulting gradient-based framework unifies tasks usually handled by separate solutions, such as reconstructing heliostat surfaces and kinematics from operational flux images without costly deflectometry, predicting irradiance at the receiver, and optimizing aim points to realize a desired receiver flux density distribution. Built on PyTorch, artist scales to real plants through GPU acceleration, a structure-of-arrays memory layout, and nested data parallelism. It interfaces with open data sources such as the PAINT database. We describe the software architecture, physical models, and optimization framework, and demonstrate the workflow on representative tasks. By integrating modeling, prediction, and optimization into a single open, interpretable package, artist provides a principled foundation for data-driven research toward autonomous solar tower operation.

**comment/C1：** 14 pages, 4 figures, abridged abstract, submitted to Machine Learning: Engineering (IOP Publishing)

</details>

**abstract/A1：** Autonomous mobile robots confront significant chal lenges in recognizing the motion properties of objects in dy namic environments. However, existing methods are hindered by limitations such as boundary ambiguity, occlusion, viewpoint constraints, and training complexity. In this paper, we propose an innovative end-to-end Multi-View Spatio-Temporal Fusion network, named MVSTF, which utilizes sequential point clouds to generate multi-view images and feature differences, and designs a multi-branch network to extract spatio-temporal and dimen sional features in parallel, and realizes high-precision moving object segmentation. First, sequential point clouds are utilized to generate multi-view images and feature differences. Then, an end-to-end multi-branch network including Dual Down-sampling Blocks (DDB), Spatial Attention Blocks (SAB), Multi-Kernel Convolutional Neural Network blocks (MKCNN), Dual Feature Fusion Blocks (DFFB), and the Point Fusion (PF) module, is designed to extract motion features from feature differences and geometric and semantic features from multi-view images. Finally, an auxiliary semantic head is introduced to further improve the algorithm's robustness and the model's interpretability. This work is validated on the SemanticKITTI and KITTI-Road bench marks, achieving state-of-the-art results on the SemanticKITTI MOS validation set and the KITTI-Road validation set, and competitive results on the hidden SemanticKITTI-MOS test set. The code is available at https://github.com/ZhouJJ111/MVSTF.

**内容简述：** 该论文提出 Accelerate Bench，包含 32 个来自科学应用与超算竞赛的 CPU 程序优化任务，用独立 verifier 对 16 个 coding agent 的加速比与正确性打分，并记录其程序与轨迹。

**排除原因：** 研究对象是应用级代码优化 agent 的执行速度与构建配置依赖，不涉及视觉证据、latent 推理状态或其使用；「单处改动价值随另一改动在 1.01x 与 6.4x 间变化」仅是表面类比于贡献分配，未提供可核查的状态、证据或训练线索。

**title/T1：** Accelerate Bench: Evaluating Agents for Application-Level Program Optimization

**abstract/A1：** Application optimization requires coding agents to discover useful changes and coordinate them across a complete program while preserving the required computation. We introduce Accelerate Bench, a benchmark of 32 CPU optimization tasks adapted from scientific applications and supercomputing competitions. Each task provides a working program and specifies the workload, correctness requirements, timing boundaries, and permitted edits, leaving agents to choose where and how to optimize. Public testing supports iterative development, and a separate verifier scores the final submission. On benchmark version 1.1, we evaluate 16 coding agents, each pairing a model with a harness. Their Score@1 ranges from 25.5% to 67.4%. Most of their programs are correct, and the size of the speedup separates them: the two leading agents are at least 2x faster on 22 or more of the 32 tasks, while the other fourteen reach 2x on 8 to 17 and leave 125 of their 412 correct outcomes below 1.25x. Controlled replays show why coordination across an application matters: identical source code runs between 0.29x and 2.12x depending only on build and runtime settings, and one code change is worth 1.01x or 6.4x depending on another. Accelerate Bench pairs executable workloads with agents' programs and trajectories to evaluate both their gains and the process behind them.

**title/T1：** Advancing Cognitive Pairwise Comparisons for Human-Centric Artificial Intelligence and Data Science: A Human-in-the-Loop Framework

**abstract/A1：** Human-centric artificial intelligence and data science (HCAD) systems increasingly involve human-in-the-loop (HITL) interventions to overcome the limitations of fully automated machine learning algorithms, such as automation bias and the inability to incorporate tacit domain knowledge, and continuously improve predictive performance. Data transformations, feature selection, feature weighting, and model selection usually require laborious human involvement across iterations of artificial intelligence and data science (AI&amp;DS) pipelines, making development a challenging and time-consuming process. The Cognitive Pairwise Comparison (CPC) framework is proposed as a human-centric methodology to elicit preferences and priorities in a structured format. To establish essential facets of human-centricity, this research advances the CPC methodology so that user preference elicitation can be systematically quantified in these challenging AI&amp;DS tasks. To demonstrate the usability and validity of these facets, this study presents several applications within movie recommender systems using the MovieLens dataset. It exemplifies how the extended CPC framework can facilitate interactions between human judgments and data across supervised learning, dimensionality reduction, and unsupervised learning algorithms.

**内容简述：** 提出 STORMGUIDE-FL 联邦优化框架，用客户端按预算采样非平稳流数据、并在本地更新层面引入服务器远程指导修正，以应对本地概念漂移与全局客户端漂移。

**排除原因：** 该文属联邦学习中的数据采样与优化纠偏，不涉及多模态推理、latent 状态生成或推理期证据获取；「更新级修正」也与 LVR 的状态更新或监督问题缺乏具体可核查的对应线索。

<details>
<summary>来源材料：标题、摘要与备注</summary>

**title/T1：** STORMGUIDE-FL: Stochastic Remote Guidance for Efficient Mining of Federated Streaming Data

**abstract/A1：** Federated Learning enables collaborative model training across distributed edge devices ("clients") while preserving data privacy. However, real-world deployments involve clients that observe continuous data streams from evolving environments while operating under strict resource limitations. Existing solutions still face two major challenges: local concept drift, where each client's data distribution shifts over time, and global client drift, arising from asynchronous engagement and imbalanced contributions across heterogeneous training participants, formally described as dual client heterogeneity. We propose STORMGUIDE-FL, a federated optimization and data-mining framework that mitigates both types of drift using a server-guided pipeline for data acquisition and local training. For data acquisition, a lightweight client-side sampling strategy incrementally selects informative and diverse instances from non-stationary, non-IID local streams under bounded memory, compute, and labeling budget. For local training, the server's remote guidance is embedded directly into local optimization as an update-level correction, counteracting client drift without discarding scarce labeled samples. We empirically verify the effectiveness of the proposed sampling strategy on federated data streams across gradual, sudden, and recurring concept drift, and demonstrate that its gains compound with the update-level drift correction. Experimental results further show improved speed and robustness of global model convergence under resource-constrained, heterogeneous conditions.

**comment/C1：** 21 pages, 7 figures, 4 tables

</details>

**研究分类：** EXCLUDE · 排除

摘要级简评；深入判断请结合原文人工阅读。

**内容简述：** 提出 FH-Sampling：先用超图刻画样本间高阶关系并自适应分配采样比例，再用离散小波变换分解频率成分，按超图引导组合相关样本的高频与目标样本的低频，以生成少数类样本，用于不平衡时间序列分类与航迹生成。

**排除原因：** 该工作是时间序列的过采样数据增强，不涉及 VLM 推理、latent 状态生成或证据使用；超图高阶关系与频率分解仅停留在样本空间合成，与 LVR 的表示、训练监督或停止决策问题缺乏可核查的具体接口。

<details>
<summary>来源材料：标题、摘要与备注</summary>

**title/T1：** FH-Sampling: Frequency-aware Hypergraph-driven Oversampling for Imbalanced Time-Series Classification

**abstract/A1：** Imbalanced time-series data appears commonly in diverse applications, such as medical diagnosis. When trained on imbalanced data, classifiers tend to exhibit a bias toward the majority class, making it difficult to identify minority-class instances accurately, despite their critical importance. Sampling techniques have proven effective in rebalancing imbalanced data. However, existing interpolation-based oversampling methods typically rely on pairwise interpolation, limiting their ability to capture high-order inter-sample relationships, and their inherent smoothing effects tend to suppress high-frequency components, compromising spectral fidelity. Therefore, we propose a Frequency-aware Hypergraph-driven Oversampling method (FH-Sampling) for imbalanced time-series classification. In FH-Sampling, a hypergraph is first constructed in the original time-series space to capture complex high-order inter-sample relationships, and sampling ratios are adaptively assigned to mitigate the impact of noisy samples. The discrete wavelet transform decomposes each sample into frequency components. Guided by the sample hypergraph, FH-Sampling combines high-frequency components from related samples while retaining the target sample's low-frequency component to help preserve important frequency characteristics. Experiments on 24 imbalanced datasets demonstrate the advantages of FH-Sampling for imbalanced time-series classification. We further apply FH-Sampling to aircraft trajectory generation. Experiments on simulated aircraft trajectories show that FH-Sampling produces trajectories that better match the real distribution, highlighting its potential for practical applications.

</details>

<details>
<summary>来源材料：标题、摘要与备注</summary>

**title/T1：** Digits in Notation Are Not Numbers: A Scoring Pitfall in PDF-to-Markdown Conversion of Japanese Technical Documents (Preliminary Evaluation)

**abstract/A1：** Converting PDFs to Markdown is now routine preprocessing for search and language models, yet scoring the numbers in the output is easy to get wrong. We evaluate MinerU, a plain-text OCR baseline (NDLOCR-Lite), and a deterministic post-processing pipeline (anchor insertion, footnote reordering, fixes of look-alike characters in fixed contexts, gated formula repair using two independent OCR partners, and heading reconstruction) on 48 public Japanese pages (three documents), text-layer and rasterized. Our pre-specified number-and-unit F1 favored the OCR baseline (0.575 vs 0.397), and a disagreement check between the two engines seemed to flag about half of the converter's number errors (54.6%). Both were artifacts. The scorer counted digits in the converter's notation (image-link paths, HTML attributes), which plain text lacks. With the notation removed (a post-hoc check), the F1 scores tie (0.575 vs 0.594), and the check flags only 13% of number errors, because most errors are misses that both engines share. What remains: the OCR baseline has a lower body character error rate (0.012 vs 0.053 rasterized). The pipeline raises extra-number recall at page level (+0.145; the document-level interval touches 0), mostly by restoring page numbers, but lowers heading-level agreement (0.133 to 0.061) and leaves spurious formulas unchanged; its formula repair never fires. A pre-specified precision gate for its flags (0.80, human-judged) is met at 0.929, yet the post-processing hypothesis fails on its improvement items. We recommend scoring numbers after removing notation and checking critical figures against the source. By the pre-specified criteria, the study stays a technical report.

**comment/C1：** Preliminary evaluation. 26 pages

</details>

**title/T1：** K2-Horizon: A Frontier Fleet of Open Source Language Models

**abstract/A1：** We present K2-Horizon, a fleet of six fully open language models, from a 0.9B dense model to a 375B-A23B MoE, built for general-purpose reasoning and agentic work across math and science, software engineering, deep research, office automation, and beyond. The models lead or are competitive with strong open models of their size on agentic and coding benchmarks. On the modeling side, to strengthen reasoning, we introduce Mixture-of-Value Attention (MoVA), applying MoE to attention value projections, and softplus attention gating, a more flexible, theoretically motivated gate. Our 36B-A4B model uses both and nearly matches a 32B dense model trained on the same data, with one-seventh the active parameters. We also introduce Uno, lossless diffusion adapters that speed up decoding by up to 2.2x without a separate draft model. Our release follows the LLM360 definition of open source for transparency and reproducibility: the full development history, including intermediate checkpoints from every training stage, pre-training data, training logs, and all training, evaluation, and infrastructure code, notably our production-scale xLLM framework for dense and MoE training and the RL360 reinforcement-learning stack. Beyond the data itself, we release and document in detail every pipeline that built it, the part of model development that open releases most rarely disclose. These pipelines produced roughly 10T synthetic pre-training tokens, showing that synthetic data can be a major ingredient of pre-training at scale. Four of the models share one 22T-token pre-training corpus and recipe, revealing consistent scaling behavior and enabling controlled studies of scale and sparsity. All artifacts are available at https://ifm.ai/k2/

**arXiv 学科：** cs.CV

[论文页面](<http://arxiv.org/abs/2611.21054v1>) · [PDF](<https://arxiv.org/pdf/2611.21054v1>)

摘要级简评；深入判断请结合原文人工阅读。

**内容简述：** 该文首次将数据蒸馏用于行级手写文本识别，以字符 n-gram 聚类定义文本伪类，并把 GM、DM、MTT 迁移到 CRNN-CTC 上，在四个数据集上发现蒸馏集均不优于真实初始行。

**排除原因：** 论文关注训练集压缩与合成样本优化，不涉及 VLM 内部视觉状态、latent 推理轨迹、证据获取或停止决策，其负结果也未提供可核查的 LVR 方法线索，故排除。

<details>
<summary>来源材料：标题、摘要与备注</summary>

**title/T1：** Dataset Distillation for Handwritten Text Recognition: An Empirical Study

**abstract/A1：** Dataset distillation (DD) replaces large training datasets with smaller synthetic ones to reduce computational costs. While traditionally used for classification, we present, to our knowledge, the first DD study for line-level handwritten text recognition (HTR). Unlike classification tasks, which use discrete labels, HTR employs unaligned sequences from a virtually infinite output space as labels. To adapt classification-based DD methods to this scenario, we define text pseudo-classes by clustering transcriptions based on character n-grams. We adapt gradient matching (GM), distribution matching (DM) and trajectory matching (MTT) to a Convolutional Recurrent Neural Network (CRNN) trained with Connectionist Temporal Classification (CTC). In this process, synthetic line images are generated by optimising only the pixels of real starting lines (either randomly chosen or selected as text medoids), while keeping their original transcriptions fixed. Across four datasets (IAM, George Washington, READ\\,2016, LAM) and three budgets (1--10\\,\\% of the training lines), no distilled set outperforms its real initialisation lines. Random lines prove better than medoids, and further optimisation only degrades recognition. Methodologically, DM lowers its objective without benefit, while GM and MTT barely move theirs. We turn these findings into guidelines for evaluating data compression in HTR.

</details>

On four manually annotated real-world mapping flights, an association-only evaluation using ground-truth detections shows that the combined weighted multi-pass approach provides the best trade-off between association quality and count error. It is integrated into the open-source web application ARGUS and visualized as verifiable, correctable object groups for first responders. https://github.com/RoblabWh/argus

<summary>来源材料：标题、摘要与备注</summary>

**title/T1：** MORE: Merge Once, Route Early for Training-Free Multi-Subject Composition from Large LoRA Pools

**abstract/A1：** Public hubs offer many personalized LoRAs per text-to-image backbone, yet composing two of them in one image remains fragile. In FLUX, keeping a pool of $K=10$ or $20$ subject LoRAs loaded makes their deltas interfere, and even loading only the two requested LoRAs keeps both subjects in fewer than 4% of images: one subject vanishes, the two fuse, or the image splits into a collage. We present MORE (Merge Once, Route Early), a training-free two-stage pipeline for FLUX. Merge once: the whole pool is folded into a single fixed-rank adapter by the subspace-regression router of SSR-Merge, made reliable by ridge, rank and calibration choices, and factored exactly into a shared part and per-subject parts. Route early: during the first 30% of the denoising steps each subject's part is gated to its layout region; a decaying soft attention bias ties every region to its own subject tokens, and a cyclic swap guidance extrapolates away from the prediction with the subjects' regions permuted, which counteracts region homogenization. On held-out seeds, MORE keeps both subjects in 94.2% ($K=10$) and 78.3% ($K=20$) of images, against 50.8% / 35.8% for FreeFuse and 25.0% / 24.2% for LoRAShop, and reaches an ImageReward of 1.32 (best baseline 0.07), while all $K$ subjects stay in one adapter. With layouts inferred automatically it still keeps both subjects in 70.0% / 55.0% of images.

</details>

**arXiv ID：** 2611.21114

**作者：** Ke Sun、Shuwei Li、Haiyang Mei、Mike Zheng Shou

**arXiv 学科：** cs.CV

[论文页面](<http://arxiv.org/abs/2611.21114v1>) · [PDF](<https://arxiv.org/pdf/2611.21114v1>)

**研究分类：** EXCLUDE · 排除

摘要级简评；深入判断请结合原文人工阅读。

**排除原因：** 该文研究利用 3D causal VAE 按时间分组解码所致的周期性保真度波动来零样本检测生成视频，属视频取证方向；虽涉及 VAE 潜空间解码保真度，但未研究 VLM 推理状态、证据获取或 latent 内容使用，与 LVR 主线缺乏实质联系。

<details>
<summary>来源材料：标题、摘要与备注</summary>

**title/T1：** VAE Rhythm: Temporal Decoding Traces for AI-Generated Video Detection

**abstract/A1：** Visible artifacts are an unreliable cue for detecting generated videos, because newer generators learn to remove them. We instead detect a trace left by the generation pipeline itself. Most video generators decode latents with a 3D causal VAE that groups consecutive frames in time, so the fidelity of generated frames rises and falls periodically with their position in a group. We call this periodic trace VAE Rhythm. Real videos are captured frame by frame and do not have it. To reveal it without training, we propose a phase scan. The scan reconstructs a clip with an off-the-shelf VAE from successive start offsets and measures the periodicity of the reconstruction error across these offsets. We find VAE Rhythm in most of the 39 variants of 31 generators we test, including the closed-source Sora, Kling 3.0 and Seedance 2.0. We use the rhythm as a zero-shot score, as a plug-in for existing detectors and as a data engine that pairs real videos with their VAE reconstructions to train our detector CaDet. On DF26, the training-free rhythm score outperforms all 15 retrained baselines, and as a plug-in it improves all 19 tested detectors by 6.7% to 23.7% AUROC. CaDet achieves the best AUROC on AIGVDBench, DF26 and three 2026 closed-source models, and its variant trained without any generated video still exceeds 90% on AIGVDBench.

**comment/C1：** 24 pages, 7 figures. Project page: https://showlab.github.io/vae-rhythm

</details>

<details>
<summary>来源材料：标题、摘要与备注</summary>

**title/T1：** IGRecon4D: Dynamic-Object-Aware Feed-Forward Reconstruction of Driving Scenes

**abstract/A1：** Feed-forward 4D driving-scene reconstruction enables efficient modeling of dynamic autonomous-driving scenes, but current methods suffer from two complementary failure modes: semantic leakage of traffic participants into the static representation and geometric drift of Gaussian locations across viewpoints. We propose \\textbf{IGRecon4D}, a feed-forward dynamic scene reconstruction framework that addresses these failures with training-time instance-prior distillation and LiDAR-anchored Gaussian positioning. Specifically, an instance-level semantic branch provides a potentially dynamic participant prior, which is distilled into dynamic-mask learning through the Instance-Dynamic Consistency Constraint to encourage high-recall localization of traffic-participant regions prone to dynamic-static leakage. In parallel, sparse LiDAR measurements guide dense depth estimation, and the resulting depths are back-projected to anchor Gaussian positions for improved multi-view geometric consistency. Experiments on the Waymo Open Dataset and zero-shot evaluation on nuScenes demonstrate improved full-image reconstruction on the main benchmark and stronger traffic-participant-region reconstruction under cross-dataset evaluation.

</details>

It covers the Lhasa River (Tibet), whose strong anthropogenic changes and diverse hydromorphological profiles make it an ideal study area. We developed two model-based neural networks: a forward-backward (FB) plug-and-play scheme and an unfolded FB scheme. We compared them against learned neural networks baselines (SwinIR, RDN) on synthetic data, on real scenes, and through a statistical test over the whole real paired Landsat-Sentinel dataset. The unfolded network achieves the highest PSNR and SSIM on the real RGB components with fast inference, offering the best trade-off between accuracy and computational cost. For NDWI-based water segmentation, its performance shows no statistically significant difference from that of the best methods.

<details>
<summary>来源材料：标题、摘要与备注</summary>

**title/T1：** Cap-Aware Boosting for Green Day-Ahead Electricity Price Forecasting

**abstract/A1：** Accurate forecasting of Green Day-Ahead Market (GDAM) electricity prices is essential for market participants in the Indian power sector. We present a LightGBM-based forecasting framework for Indian Energy Exchange GDAM prices, which clear in 96 fifteen-minute intervals per day. The proposed system explicitly models price-cap behavior by separating capped-price events from normal market conditions. A classification head estimates the probability of the regulatory price cap (Rs 10,000/MWh), while a regression head predicts uncapped prices in logarithmic space. Final forecasts are obtained through probabilistic blending of these components and are accompanied by nine quantile forecasts for uncertainty estimation. Evaluated on 257 trading days between 1 January and 14 September 2026, the model achieves a mean absolute error (MAE) of 397.9 Rs/MWh and a mean absolute percentage error (MAPE) of 9.57%, substantially outperforming a Chronos-2 baseline (583.3 MAE) and a persistence baseline using the previous day's profile (589.1 MAE). We further introduce leak-safe variants that incorporate real-time market signals, unmatched sell volumes, and solar generation proxies. In a recent out-of-sample evaluation, the quantile-clock variant achieved the best short-term performance with an MAE of 789 Rs/MWh during 25-28 October, while the enhanced capped-price model achieved an MAE of 716 Rs/MWh across 21 evaluation days through 16 November. These results demonstrate the effectiveness of regime-aware probabilistic forecasting for high-volatility electricity markets.

**abstract/A1：** Self-supervised pretraining has transformed language and vision, but its application to functional MRI (fMRI) is constrained by data access. The largest standardized fMRI resources are governed by data use agreements and dominated by a small number of acquisition protocols, while the thousands of openly licensed datasets on OpenNeuro are individually small, heterogeneously organized, and unprocessed. We present the first release of Open-fMIND, a uniformly preprocessed, openly accessible corpus of parcellated fMRI timeseries from 322 OpenNeuro studies, comprising 11,379 subjects and 45,731 functional runs. Each run is preprocessed with fMRIPrep and parcellated under 52 atlases spanning 14 families, yielding a massive 2.4 million timeseries. Timeseries are released either denoised with our default pipeline (preproc) or as the fMRIPrep output with its confound files (quasiraw), with functional connectivity matrices, per-run provenance and motion metadata. Open-fMIND is intended as a pretraining resource for self-supervised brain representation learning. Pretraining on it yields downstream performance comparable to that obtained with UK Biobank.

摘要级简评；深入判断请结合原文人工阅读。

**内容简述：** 提出 MiSTiQ，用 trellis 编码加 beam search 在有限码本下编码 KV cache，并推导 MX-Hash 使重建值直接落在 microscaling 低精度格式上，从而在约 1.25 比特/元素的极低码率下兼顾困惑度与下游准确率。

**排除原因：** 论文只处理纯文本 LLM 推理的 KV cache 压缩与低精度计算，未涉及视觉或多模态推理状态的内容保留、生成方式、监督或停止决策；虽然「压缩 latent 状态存储」与 LVR 的成本议题表面相关，但原文没有可核查的状态保真度或推理行为线索，故不入选。

<details>
<summary>来源材料：标题、摘要与备注</summary>

**title/T1：** MiSTiQ: MicroScaling Trellis Quantization for Extreme KV Cache Compression

**abstract/A1：** Modern large language models (LLMs) increasingly support longer contexts and serve more concurrent requests, increasing both sequence lengths and batch sizes. Both trends increase KV-cache size and memory traffic during inference. KV-cache quantization reduces these costs, with recent approaches using codebook-based vector quantization to achieve extremely low bit widths. However, hardware constraints limit codebook size, and most methods reconstruct the cache in higher-precision floating-point formats for attention, limiting the computational benefits of quantization. To address these limitations, we introduce MiSTiQ, a drop-in replacement for codebook-based vector quantizers that combines trellis-coded storage with microscaling (MX) formats for low-precision computation. We combine trellis quantization with beam search to encode the KV cache over large reconstruction spaces without large codebooks. To support MX computation, we derive MX-Hash functions that generate reconstruction values directly in the target MX element format. These functions use the scale-conditioned marginal distribution of block-normalized Gaussian inputs. On Llama3 and Qwen3, MiSTiQ achieves lower WikiText perplexity and higher GSM8K accuracy than the evaluated baselines across several block-scale formats at approximately 1.25 effective bits per element. With NVFP4, it also achieves the highest LongBench average on both models.
